_readme: Questions and answers for the New Here page (rendered as accessible accordions and as FAQPage structured data for search engines). TO ADD: copy an object, write a plain-language question and a short warm answer. Keep answers pastoral and factual; anything sacramental should be checked with the chaplain.

faqs.q: Do I have to be Catholic to come?
faqs.a: No. Mass, dinners, talks and socials are open to everyone - Catholic, other traditions, exploring, or just curious. Nobody will quiz you.

faqs.q: Can I come alone if I don't know anyone?
faqs.a: Yes, and many people do exactly that. If you'd like, contact us before you come and a executive member will meet you at the door so you walk in with a friendly face.
Whatever you'd wear to class is fine. People come straight from lectures, labs and sport.
Confession and quiet adoration from 5:00 pm, Mass at 6:00 pm (about 45mins to 1hr), then students head off to Friday Fellowship (usually in the Kambri Chaplaincy Room).

faqs.q: I'm not sure about receiving Communion - is that okay?
faqs.a: Completely. If you aren't in a state of grace, or aren't Catholic, feel free to stay in your seat or you are welcome to come forward with arms crossed for a blessing.

faqs.q: Is there a cost or membership requirement?
faqs.a: No - everything regular is free and open. Formal membership (via Rubric) supports the Society and gets you voting rights and member perks, but it is never required to attend.

faqs.q: I'm an international or postgraduate student - is this for me?
faqs.a: Very much so. The Society spans undergrads, postgrads, international students and staff, and Mass is the same in every country - it's one of the fastest ways to find your feet in Canberra.

faqs.q: I've been away from the Church for a while. Where do I start?
faqs.a: Just come to Mass, or message us and ask to speak with the chaplain - no explanations required. Confession is available every Friday if and when you want it.

faqs.q: I'm not baptised but I'm curious about becoming Catholic. What's the path?
faqs.a: The path is called OCIA (the Order of Christian Initiation of Adults), run with the local parish - ten catechumens have come through the Society in the current year alone. Start with a conversation: email us or speak with the chaplain, any time of year.
